prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 街道便民服务中心一窗受理事项办理台账 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 3 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "序号" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 31px
  col 2: header "状态" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 46px
  col 3: header "内容" · longest unbreakable word 31px · one-line width 1932px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 720px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A working ledger for street-level one-window service cases, used to locate a case by 序号, check its 状态, and read the narrative 内容.","reading":"Readers scan the short left-hand metadata first, then read each 内容 row as a unit; cross-row comparison is mainly on 状态, while 内容 is read sequentially. The content is about 1932px on one line, so 500–600px still gives roughly four lines and metadata can be widened without much height penalty.","groups":["序号 and 状态 belong together as a compact left metadata block because both are short row-level labels","内容 stands alone as the substantive record and needs the remaining width"],"keep_intact":["序号 values and the 状态 labels 已办结/办理中/已退回/待补正","dates such as 3月12日 and 4月8日","permit/licence numbers, amounts, names and other case identifiers inside 内容"],"may_wrap":["the long 内容 narrative at Chinese punctuation and phrase boundaries","long addresses, agency names and document titles when necessary"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[52,67,600],"idea":"Content-maximising: give 序号 and 状态 only their exact one-line fit and leave all remaining width to the narrative."},{"name":"B","widths":[52,144,523],"idea":"Status-led: keep 序号 minimal but widen 状态 into a clear comparison band, accepting a slightly narrower content column that still wraps to about four lines."},{"name":"C","widths":[80,120,519],"idea":"Reference-led: give both metadata columns generous fixed widths for easy row lookup and future longer labels, while content remains the dominant column at about four lines."}]}
